correctness.rationale: All 338 nonzero endpoint-localized signed integral boundary blocks were enumerated, their compositions verified zero, and all Smith pivots were units. Using the established girth-six diagonal rank H_(4,4)=104 and an explicit oriented-edge basis, the equivariant Euler-Poincare identity computes trace H_(3,4) from fixed chain generators. All 5616 projectivities and their action on the incidence graph were enumerated exactly; their 2808/72/0 trace values equal the independently enumerated ordered-triangle permutation character for every element. Type-swapping automorphisms have trace zero on both modules. Equality of rational characters implies the full 11232-element group module isomorphism. Six distinct fixed-point profiles were rechecked by a separate endpoint-indexed trace calculation. No general-in-q assertion is made.

originality.rationale: The previously published all-order projective-plane result (fully read) proves the endpoint q^2 rank, and therefore already covers the 2808 numerical total; the new claim is the previously unreported rational collineation/polarity representation. Neither that full prior proof nor the inspected Asao-Hiraoka-Kanazawa and Gu papers state or imply the 72-on-involutions character, the triangle permutation isomorphism, or the invariant-space conclusion. Siemons-Smith uses subspace-poset incidence homology, not graph-metric magnitude homology. Exact and alias database queries found no covering theorem; unindexed equivalence remains possible.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent group representation in other mathematical literature may exist.
The isomorphism is rational and abstract, not an explicit equivariant chain map or integral lattice identification.
The matrix checker handles precisely the finite projective plane of order three, not all projective planes.

value.rationale: The known endpoint dimensions do not encode the action of projective collineations on magnitude cycles. This result determines the complete 11232-element rational symmetry module as one transitive coset representation of a four-element triangle stabilizer, including an explicit sparse character and one invariant line. It is a canonical finite-geometric object and a reproducible nontrivial structural refinement, not an arbitrary coefficient change or rank recomputation.
